newsitem.title: USA: Democrats press for ethanol subsidy in US tax bill.
newsitem.headline: Democrats press for ethanol subsidy in US tax bill.

text.p: Democratic leaders on Wednesday asked congressional tax bill writers to extend the ethanol subsidy program through 2007, as called for in the Senate version of proposed tax legislation.

Sen. Tom Daschle and Rep. Dick Gephardt said in a letter that the loss of the subsidy would mean reduced prices for corn, soybeans and sorghum by as much as 16 cents per bushel and jeopardize farmer-owned ethanol production facilities.
The House version of the tax bill would drop the ethanol subsidy by 2000, while the Senate version would keep the program in place through 2007.

"It is vitally important to keep this proven program in place, and to do that, the Archer provision needs to be eliminated from the bill," Daschle said in the letter to Bill Archer, chairman of the House ways and means committee and to William Roth, chairman of the Senate finance committee.

House and Senate negotiators will begin meeting later this week to work out differences in their tax and spending bills, with the aim of sending final legislation to President Clinton before the August recess.
